title: Escarpment and Trail
premise: Astrid Vane chases storms across the high escarpments to pay off the Meridian Syndicate, cheerful lenders who break legs with a smile. When the prospector Elias Thorn dies in her truck after trading her a map to the river's forbidden source, she inherits his promise: deliver the map to a daughter he abandoned in the valley town of Kestrel's Ford. Pursued by Syndicate collectors and Thorn's old partners, Astrid and the daughter, Wren, follow the river upstream through canyons, ghost camps, and a storm that floods the gorge, discovering the 'source' is a lost silver lode Thorn hid to protect the valley from being strip-mined. At the source, Astrid must choose between selling the map to clear her debt and burning it to keep Wren's home whole; she burns it, settles the debt by turning the Syndicate's own ledgers over to a federal marshal, and finally stops moving, finding belonging in Kestrel's Ford.
about_author: Yara Ishikawa is a former river guide who spent six seasons running rapids in the northern ranges before turning to writing full-time. Her fiction blends hard-edged wilderness adventure with quiet stories of people building families from strangers.

chapters.title: Weather Debt
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Chasing a supercell across the escarpment, she calculates storm paths and loan interest in the same notebook. The Meridian Syndicate's collectors find her at a gas station, all smiles and threats, resetting her deadline. Emotional beat: restless dread — she drives through the night because stopping is the only thing she truly fears.

chapters.title: The Man Who Flagged Her Down
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On a flooded back road she finds Elias Thorn shot and half-drowned. He offers a oilcloth-wrapped map in exchange for a promise: take it to his daughter in Kestrel's Ford. He dies before dawn. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion — Astrid, who never promises anything, hears herself say yes.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, opening with Thorn's dying flashback. She studies the map, finds a second document — Thorn's ledger implicating his old partners and the Syndicate in a rigged claim. Collectors reach the gas station where she slept. Emotional beat: trapped realization that the promise has made her a target.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Ford
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The valley town is poor, proud, and watchful. She locates Wren Thorn, a ferocious young ferry operator who wants nothing from her father. Astrid withholds the truth of his death. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reads Astrid instantly as a liar and a drifter, but recognizes the map's handwriting and agrees to travel — for answers, not company. They leave before the Syndicate's second collector, Voss, arrives. Emotional beat: guarded alliance born of mutual need.

chapters.title: The First Rapid
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Running the gorge in Wren's battered boat, they survive a sweep through whitewater and learn each other's skills. Astrid admits the map was bought with a dying man's last breath. Emotional beat: first flicker of trust on the water.

chapters.title: Optimists with Ledgers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Voss catches up at an abandoned trading post, offering to forgive Astrid's debt if she hands over the map and the girl. She stalls; Wren overhears the offer. Emotional beat: shame of her own history colliding with the fear of losing the first person who stayed.

chapters.title: Ghost Camp at Miller's Bend
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a silver-rush ghost town they find Thorn's old partners' camp, recently used — someone else is following the river. They recover Thorn's hidden assay samples proving the lode runs under the town itself. Emotional beat: the map stops being treasure and becomes a weapon aimed at home.

chapters.title: The Story of a Coward
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, framed as a night-fire telling. Through Thorn's letters, Wren learns he abandoned the valley to draw the Syndicate's claim away from his family — not from weakness, but failed protection. Emotional beat: grief reframed; anger softening into something like forgiveness.

chapters.title: Voss Closes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ambushed at a portage, Astrid trades a beating for Wren's escape downstream, then turns the tables using storm-reading skill, trapping Voss's crew above a rising river. Emotional beat: Astrid chooses the fight instead of the exit — the first time she stops running.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm system Astrid predicted floods the gorge early. They run the river at flood stage to stay ahead of the partners' expedition, nearly losing the boat and the map. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce, wordless partnership.

chapters.title: The Partners
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The old partners — led by the courteous, ruthless Halloran — corner them and reveal the full scheme: Thorn's ledger, the Syndicate's money, and a strip-mine permit that dies if the source stays hidden. Halloran offers Astrid everything she owes. Emotional beat: temptation laid out in exact numbers.

chapters.title: Split Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, believing Astrid will sell, takes the map and slips away at night, planning to reach the source alone and destroy it. Emotional beat: heartbreak as loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions — she trusts Astrid's honesty, not her strength.

chapters.title: Alone Upstream
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid climbs out of the gorge alone, past Syndicate checkpoints, using the storm to cover her trail. She confronts what she's been fleeing: not the debt, but the belief that she's unlovable when still. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won self-recognition.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reaches the river's head: a hidden canyon spring above the lode, marked by Thorn's cairn. Halloran's crew arrives; she is trapped with the map she meant to destroy. Emotional beat: courage without backup — the daughter finishing the father's stand.

chapters.title: Escarpment
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid descends the escarpment ahead of a supercell she's tracked for two days, arriving at the source as the storm breaks. Emotional beat: the chaser finally arriving — running toward, not away.

chapters.title: The Storm at the Head of the River
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. In the flood and lightning, Astrid and Wren turn Halloran's own expedition gear against his crew, and Astrid burns the map in the storm while Thorn's ledger goes to a marshal Voss's defection summoned. Halloran is taken by the river he meant to own. Emotional beat: the promise kept in fire and water.

chapters.title: What the Map Was Worth
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The Syndicate, its ledgers exposed, settles: her debt is voided in exchange for testimony. Astrid expects to leave. Emotional beat: the strange vertigo of having no reason to run.

chapters.title: Ferryman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren buries her father's letters at the spring and reopens the ferry with Astrid as partner. The town that watched the stranger now sets a plate for her. Emotional beat: belonging arriving without being asked for.

chapters.title: Still Water
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid stays through a whole season for the first time in years, learning that stopping doesn't cost — it pays. A Syndicate remnant sends one last letter; she reads it by the fire, unafraid, and burns it. Emotional beat: peace as an active choice.

chapters.title: The Next Storm
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm builds over the escarpment and Astrid loads the truck — but this time Wren rides along, and they'll be back by dark. Chasing becomes a trade, not an escape. Emotional beat: joy; found family in motion.

chapters.title: Source and Mouth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, coda. At the river's mouth, Astrid and Wren scatter the last of Thorn's ashes where the water ends. Astrid finally tells the whole truth of his death; Wren finally says the word 'family.' Emotional beat: the river, the promise, and the two of them — all arrived.
